main_text.head: EXERC. XX.

head.i: VTRVM CORRVPTIO ET PVTREFACTIO sint totius substantiæ morbi.

main_text.p: Postmodum Fernelius eodem capite decimo, libri secundi, de Abditis rerum causis morbum, quem totius substantiæ corruptelam appellat, duplicem statuit, unum simplicem corruptionem, alterum putredine.Simplex corruptio: corruptio (inquit) est spiritus, innatiq; caloris (qui præcipua est partis substantia) dissipatio, aut extinctio.Per vigilias, per labores, per inedias, atrocesq; dolores spiritus dissipatur: Calor autem insitus extinguitur, in strangulatu & in penetrabili extremoq; frigore.Putredo est substantiæ partis dissolutio: talis est in gagrena, & sphacelo, in phthisi, in iecoris, lienis aliarumq; partium corruptela.Hæc Fernelius, ad quę singula nobis breuiter respondendum.

Primum simplicem corruptionem, quam spiritus innatiq; caloris dissipationem, aut extinctionem esse ait, non esse morbum formæ partis similaris patet: quandoquidem partis similaris forma nō est spiritus, neq; innatus calor.Nam

page.notes: The right margin marks (,,) beside several lines are printed marks, not words, so they are left out. "gagrena" is read as printed. "quę" and "simplicē" are read from the printed accents, which are faint. The paragraph ends at the page foot with "Nam", and the catchword "forma" follows.
